results.hypothesis: To determine whether probability calibration methods (Platt Scaling, Isotonic Regression) exhibit significantly higher Expected Calibration Error (ECE) when applied to heavily imbalanced real-world tabular data (UCI Credit Approval, UCI German Credit) compared to their performance on balanced benchmarks (AG News, 20 Newsgroups).
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: ECE values obtained from applying the same calibration methods to the balanced benchmark datasets (AG News, 20 Newsgroups) using identical models and preprocessing steps.
results.success_criteria: If ECE values are significantly higher for the imbalanced datasets compared to the balanced ones when using the same calibration methods, the hypothesis is supported. If ECE values are similar or lower for imbalanced datasets, the hypothesis is refuted.
results.notes: Uncalibrated ECE: 0.0090, Platt Scaling ECE: 0.0196, Isotonic Regression ECE: 0.0075. Interpretation depends on comparison with balanced benchmarks.
results.methodological_validity: synthetic surrogate data — the pipeline is exercised but the findings are NOT interpretable as evidence for or against the hypothesis
results.verdict_withheld_because: One or more inputs are synthetic surrogates, so these metrics describe the pipeline's behaviour on generated data and say nothing about the real-world hypothesis. See data_provenance.json.

fix_history.error_summary: load_data() assumes its data will be present: line 6: read_csv(...) reads a local file with no try/except around it, so the experiment dies if that file doesn't exist. Wrap the read, log the failure, and fall back to a small synthesized stand-in dataset (recording that in assumptions_made and the README) — or fetch the data over HTTP instead
assumptions_made: The UCI Credit Approval dataset is representative of the imbalanced real-world tabular data mentioned in the hypothesis
Using 3-fold cross-validation for calibration is sufficient for this experiment's purposes
Binning approach with 10 bins is adequate for ECE calculation

The experiment focuses on demonstrating the effect of calibration on imbalanced data rather than direct comparison with balanced benchmarks as originally planned, since only the imbalanced dataset is provided
Logistic regression is an appropriate baseline model for this type of data
The comparison is made within the same dataset (imbalanced) rather than against balanced benchmarks as originally planned
